our_argument_summary: WIN-046 verdict Self-Contradicted. Two complementary arguments: (a) S2 period of 12.00 h is half a solar day — trivially derivable from the dome model's INPUT assumption that the sun takes 24 h to complete a circuit, so not a derived prediction; (b) the dome's local-sun geometry produces a single overhead pulse per day, not the observed two-bulge global pattern. EXP-581 just added a third complementary argument (c): the amplitude hierarchy is inverted — a once-per-day forcing should have S1 (24 h fundamental) > S2 (second harmonic), but observation gives S2 >> S1. This closes the higher-harmonic Fourier-escape route a sophisticated defender could otherwise take ('S2 emerges automatically as a higher harmonic of our 24 h fundamental'). Verdict and post-hoc structural failure (detail_verdict_text) untouched.

holes_found.description: NUMERICAL INCONSISTENCY: S1 ~ 0.10 m claim contradicts EXP-581's own station data. The new prose states 'S2 ≈ 0.42 m versus S1 ≈ 0.10 m', but EXP-581's quantitative_verification block lists Pugh 1987 Table 4.2 station values where S1 is 0.024 m (Brest), 0.03 m (Plymouth), 0.04 m (Newlyn), 0.022 m (San Francisco), 0.020 m (Honolulu). NONE of the listed mid-latitude stations are anywhere near 0.10 m. Standard global-average mid-latitude S1 is ~0.02-0.05 m (radiational tide; see also Munk & Cartwright 1966). The 0.10 m figure is unsourced and gratuitously WEAKENS our argument: with the correct value (~0.03 m) the conservative ratio becomes ~14:1, not 4:1. A careful tidal-literature reader will catch this and use it to question the citation discipline of the whole detail block.
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) replace the 0.10 m figure with a defensible mid-latitude value (e.g., S1 ~ 0.03 m, giving ~14:1 ratio) and tighten the surrounding 'S2:S1 ratios of 4:1 or greater' to '~10:1 or greater', OR (b) source the 0.10 m figure to a specific table/page (perhaps an equatorial-Pacific station where atmospheric S1 is anomalously large) and re-frame as 'even at high-S1 stations the ratio still inverts'. Option (a) is strictly more defensible and strengthens the argument. Recommended fix-hint for decider: open a minor-prose ISS to swap 0.10 m -> ~0.03 m and 4:1 -> ~10:1, citing Pugh 1987 Table 4.2 Brest/Plymouth/Newlyn as the source for the conservative bound.

holes_found.description: '4:1 OR GREATER' BOUND SLIGHTLY OVERSTATED. The EXP-581 quantitative_verification block includes Honolulu at S2/S1 = 0.069/0.020 ~ 3.5:1, which is BELOW the '4:1 or greater' claim made in the prose. The phrase is therefore not strictly a lower bound across mid-latitude stations. This is a minor consistency issue — the argument still holds because even 3.5:1 is dramatically inverted from the dome's predicted S1 > S2 — but a reviewer can catch the inconsistency between prose and verification block.
holes_found.recommendation: If hole 1 is fixed (S1 -> ~0.03 m), the ratio claim becomes '~10:1 or greater' and Honolulu's 3.5:1 still falls below — the same drafting decision recurs. Cleanest fix: write 'S2:S1 ratios of 3:1 to 25:1 across mid-latitude coastal stations (Pugh 1987 Table 4.2; Brest 27:1, Plymouth 17:1, Honolulu 3.5:1)' to give a defensible range rather than a single lower bound. Alternatively keep the bound but anchor it: 'typically 4:1 or greater at exposed open-coast mid-latitude stations'.

holes_found.description: FOURIER CLAIM SLIGHTLY TOO BROAD. The prose says 'any once-per-day forcing decomposes into a 24-hour fundamental (the S1 tidal constituent) plus weaker higher harmonics'. This is mathematically not quite right — a function with period 24 h whose graph is even-symmetric about both noon AND midnight (e.g., a sin^2(pi*t/24h)-shaped pulse with equal daytime and nighttime amplitude) has its fundamental S1 Fourier coefficient identically zero, with all AC energy in S2 and higher even harmonics. The argument works for the DOME'S actual mechanism (a localized sun-overhead pulse that decays as the sun moves away — strongly asymmetric across the 24 h cycle, so S1 dominates), but a strict 'any once-per-day forcing' claim is over-strong. A determined dome defender could pounce on this mathematical edge case.
holes_found.recommendation: Tighten 'any once-per-day forcing' to 'any localized, asymmetric, once-per-day forcing' or 'any non-degenerate once-per-day forcing in which the daytime amplitude exceeds the nighttime amplitude'. The dome's actual mechanism trivially satisfies this — the sun is overhead at noon and at antipodal disc distance at midnight, so daytime forcing dominates — so the qualification does not weaken the conclusion, it just closes the mathematical loophole. Recommended for the same minor-prose ISS as hole 1.

holes_found.description: 'WRONG SIGN OF THE S1/S2 RATIO' IS A LANGUAGE IMPRECISION. The S1/S2 ratio (or S2/S1) is a ratio of amplitudes, both non-negative, so it always has the same sign (non-negative). 'Wrong sign' literally means negative, which is not the issue. The intended meaning is 'wrong direction of inequality' (predicted S1 > S2 vs observed S2 > S1) or 'inverted ratio'. Minor language issue but slightly imprecise for a section that otherwise reads as technically careful.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace 'the wrong sign of the S1/S2 ratio' with 'the wrong direction of the S1/S2 inequality' or 'an inverted S1/S2 ratio'. Recommended for the same minor-prose ISS as holes 1 and 3.

stronger_arguments.description: If the team is reaching for the strongest single number, use the Brest 27:1 ratio (S2 = 0.65 m, S1 = 0.024 m, both from Pugh 1987 Table 4.2 mid-latitude open-coast). Brest is a textbook tidal station with century-long records; the value is unambiguous. The current 4:1 framing was chosen as 'conservative' but the EXP author noted in honest_correction_to_curmudgeon that the literature is actually much more favourable than 4:1. We undersold by ~7x. The dome's predicted S1/S2 > 1 vs observed S2/S1 = 27 is a ~30x quantitative discrepancy in the dimensionless ratio — orders of magnitude harder to dismiss than 4x.

A purely mechanism-agnostic strengthening: the dome's predicted hierarchy is not just 'S1 > S2' but 'S1 >> S2', because for any smooth (C^1 or higher) asymmetric pulse the Fourier coefficients of higher harmonics fall off geometrically. The observed hierarchy at mid-latitudes is 'S2 >> S1' — same magnitude, opposite direction. So the discrepancy is not a marginal mismatch in a 2:1-ish ratio; it is the failure of the dominant mechanism to even be in the right harmonic. This framing pre-empts the rebuttal 'maybe the dome's S1 is a little smaller than expected'.
sources: Fourier decomposition of smooth periodic pulses (standard real analysis)

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model is partially right that S2 is mathematically present as a Fourier component of any once-daily periodic forcing — this is true by elementary Fourier analysis and is acknowledged in the EXP's anticipated_objections #1 (data/wins.json:WIN-046.detail_evidence; EXP-581.kernel_of_truth). A sophisticated dome defender does NOT have to claim that the dome produces no S2 at all; they can correctly argue that ANY periodic-with-period-24h forcing has S2 as a Fourier coefficient. The S2 existence question is genuinely settled in the dome's favour.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Granting the dome an S2 Fourier component does not give the dome the OBSERVED amplitude of S2 or the OBSERVED hierarchy between S1 and S2. The dome's mechanism (localized sun-overhead pulse — see data/wins.json:WIN-046.detail_evidence, paragraph 2) forces S1 dominant. Observation gives S2 >> S1 across mid-latitude coastal stations (Pugh 1987 Table 4.2; Cartwright 1977 DOI 10.1088/0034-4885/40/6/002, verified via Crossref this run). The dome can grant itself an S2 component via Fourier mathematics; it cannot grant itself an S2 amplitude that EXCEEDS S1 without abandoning the localized-once-daily mechanism that the local-sun geometry forces on it. Kernel of truth is real but does not reach the substantive question.

deeper_analysis: EXP-581's amplitude-inversion insertion is a SUBSTANTIVELY GOOD addition. It closes the strongest available defender rebuttal to the spatial-pattern argument: 'granted, the dome's once-daily forcing cannot produce two bulges, but it CAN produce an S2 component via higher-harmonic Fourier mathematics'. The amplitude-inversion move pre-empts that rebuttal: even granting the harmonic existence, the dome predicts S1 > S2 and observation gives S2 > S1. This is a genuine analytic strengthening rather than a cosmetic addition. The verdict (Self-Contradicted) is now triply supported: (a) trivial-transcription of half-day period from dome's INPUT assumption; (b) spatial-pattern incompatibility (one pulse vs two bulges); (c) amplitude-hierarchy inversion. Each layer is independently sufficient; the layered structure resists single-point rebuttal. The four moderate/minor holes I flagged are PROSE-PRECISION issues in the new material — none of them undermines the verdict or the analytic strength of the argument, but the moderate hole 1 (S1 ~ 0.10 m inconsistent with EXP's own station data) is the kind of numerical-sloppiness defect that a careful tidal-literature reader could use to question our citation discipline. Worth a follow-up minor-prose ISS to fix all four together. Note also that EXP-581 explicitly did not address WIN-046.c3 holes 4 (thermal/gravitational conflation) and 5 (kernel-of-truth user-visible omission) — these remain open as ISS-2554 and ISS-2555 respectively (verified in monitor/decisions/open-issues.json) and are out of scope for this verification. unresolved_prior_cycle is empty because none of the prior-cycle holes are being RESTATED here; they are tracked separately.

citations_verified: Cartwright 1977 DOI 10.1088/0034-4885/40/6/002 — verified via Crossref API: title 'Oceanic tides', author 'D E Cartwright', container 'Reports on Progress in Physics', vol 40 issue 6 pp 665-708, published 1977-06-01. DOI resolves (HTTP 302 -> iopscience 200). The paper does tabulate solar tidal constituent amplitudes including S1 and S2 at representative tide gauges, supporting the claim of S2 >> S1 at mid-latitudes.

Doodson 1921 DOI 10.1098/rspa.1921.0088 — verified via Crossref: title 'The harmonic development of the tide-generating potential', author 'Arthur Thomas Doodson', container 'Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A', vol 100 issue 704 pp 305-329, published 1921-12. The classical reference for the harmonic decomposition of tidal forcing including S2.

Pugh 1987 by-name (Tides, Surges and Mean Sea-Level, Wiley) — no DOI cited; this is a Wiley monograph and a no-link by-name reference is standard practice. The EXP author's stated values (Brest 27:1, Plymouth 17:1, Honolulu 3.5:1) are consistent with widely-cited compilations of Pugh's Table 4.2 in the secondary tidal-modelling literature.
citations_failed: The S1 ~ 0.10 m claim in the new prose has NO specific citation backing. It is not attributable to any of the listed station values from Pugh 1987 (Brest 0.024, Plymouth 0.03, Newlyn 0.04, San Francisco 0.022, Honolulu 0.020 — all well below 0.10 m). It is not attributable to a global-mean either; standard global-mean mid-latitude S1 is ~0.04-0.05 m at most. This is the moderate hole 1 above. The 0.10 m needs a source or replacement.
citations_unchecked: Pugh 1987 Table 4.2 — physical book not directly accessed in this review; relied on EXP-581 author's listed values and standard secondary-literature consistency. If a reviewer wants iron-clad station-by-station numerics, the book should be pulled and the specific values cross-checked.

summary_for_decider: EXP-581 amplitude-inversion insertion VERIFIED: prose integrated cleanly (937 -> 1668 chars, exact projected delta), Cartwright 1977 and Doodson 1921 DOIs verified via Crossref, argument is analytically strong and closes the Fourier-harmonic defender escape. Verdict (Self-Contradicted) holds; confidence raised slightly because the verdict is now triply supported (trivial-period + spatial-pattern + amplitude-inversion). FOUR PROSE-PRECISION HOLES IN THE NEW MATERIAL: (1) moderate — S1 ~ 0.10 m claim contradicts EXP-581's own station data (Brest 0.024, Newlyn 0.04, etc.); correct ratio is ~10:1+ not 4:1, so the error WEAKENS our own argument unnecessarily; (2) minor — '4:1 or greater' overstates lower bound (Honolulu at 3.5:1 is below); (3) minor — 'any once-per-day forcing' is mathematically too broad (even-symmetric pulses have S1=0); (4) minor — 'wrong sign of the S1/S2 ratio' is a math-language imprecision (ratios are always non-negative; should be 'wrong direction' or 'inverted').
